subject: Default capture, visibility, suppression options and deletion playbook
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@quantumhealth.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify what 'default capture' actually keeps (prompts vs outputs) — urgent for procurement

Hi Mina,

We're finalizing our procurement checklist and need a precise answer for legal. Two quick questions so our privacy team can sign off:
1) For hosted Redwood API calls, what is the default retention window for: (a) user-submitted prompts/requests, and (b) model-generated outputs/responses?
2) When streaming responses (token-by-token), are partial streamed tokens stored or only the final assembled response?

Can you also point me to an evidence artifact (SOC2/diagram) showing where EU-region request data is stored and how deletion is triggered? We attached the SOC2 checklist for reference.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Turner
Head of Vendor Risk — Quantum Health
Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify what 'default capture' actually keeps (prompts vs outputs) — urgent for procurement

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: hosted defaults differ by artifact class and by feature (streaming vs final output). Below is a concise summary plus the procedural steps to request suppression or expedited erasure.

Summary (hosted, default):
- Prompts/requests (user input): retained for 30 days by default for operational troubleshooting.
- Final model outputs/responses: retained for 90 days by default to support quality monitoring and regression alerts.
- Streaming tokens: transient; the runtime assembles the stream in-memory and only the final output is eligible for persistent capture under the policy. Partial tokens are not persisted as separate artifacts.
- KV cache and ephemeral session state: not stored to long-term logs unless the customer explicitly exports a session artifact.

EU residency note: requests from EU-region customers are routed to EU-hosted clusters by default; data-at-rest for retained logs is stored in EU regions (we maintain region-tagged buckets and audit trails). Evidence artifacts: see the shared Drive (link below) for the architecture diagram and SOC2 appendix.

Erasure and suppression paths:
- Self-service API toggle: customers can set "data_capture": false on a per-client or per-route basis to stop retaining new prompts/responses.
- Retention override: customers can lower retention to 0 days (no persistent retention) via Console -> Data settings (account admin).
- Expedited erase: submit a support ticket with GDPR/data subject request details; default turnaround is 7 business days for hosted accounts.
- Audit trail: all erase requests generate an immutable audit record (timestamp, operator, request id).

I'll loop Kim to confirm the SOC artifacts and provide a doc link and the deletion playbook. If you want a statement for contract language, we can draft an insert that says: "Default: prompts retained 30 days, outputs retained 90 days; customer may opt out via capture flag or set retention to 0."

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Trust & Privacy Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify what 'default capture' actually keeps (prompts vs outputs) — follow up and evidence pack

Hi Sophie,

Attaching the evidence pack you requested and a short playbook your security team can plug into procurement. Quick clarifications based on Mina's summary:
- The 30/90 default split exists to balance rapid incident troubleshooting (30d for inputs) with ML quality monitoring (90d for outputs).
- Streaming: we log a single assembled response artifact if capture is enabled; intermediate tokens are not written to persistent logs or object storage.
- Backups: snapshot backups are retention-aware and will not extend retention windows for logs (we prune snapshots containing logs consistent with the primary retention).

Attachments (linked): SOC2_summary.pdf, sample_prompt_responses.csv (anonymized examples showing what captured records look like).

Operational steps we recommend for procurement language:
1) Include a capture flag (boolean) in the contract that allows you to disable retention for your routes.
2) For particularly sensitive prompts, require "zero-retention" routing and validate with an on-boarding checklist.
3) Add a 7-business-day SLA for deletions and require evidence of audit record creation.

If helpful, Rishi can run a quick tenant demo showing how to flip capture off and confirm no persistent artifacts are created.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
Attachments: sample_prompt_responses.csv
